items.title: Image viewer with shuffle navigation while keeping normal navigation
items.body:
It is a feature that to this day I have only seen in ACDSee, at least in old versions. It had two keys/buttons to go back and forth in the shuffled list (not random, so that no image is shown twice and the shuffled images are always in the same order) and it also kept the usual back and forth keys/buttons to traverse the original ordered list.

Does this exist? I tried Phototonic, Geeqie, XnView and mpv --shuffle

items.title: R package to estimate threshold model - TARMA - where threshold variable is different from the dependent variable
items.body:
I wish to estimate the following threshold regression:

$$ \Delta Y_t = c_1 + \Phi_1(L) \Delta Y_{t-1} + \Theta_1(L) \epsilon_t if CDR_{t-1}=0 $$

and

$$ \Delta Y_t = c_2 + \Phi_2(L) \Delta Y_{t-1} + \Theta_2(L) \epsilon_t if CDR_{t-1}>0 $$

CDR = Current Depth of Recession = Historical Max of $Y_t$ - $Y_t$

I have seen:

  • tsDyn This package can estimate Threshold Autogressions without a moving average term, but with an arbitrary thresholding variable.

  • tseriesTARMA This package can estimate Threshold Autogressions with a moving average term, but it can only accept thresholding variable as a lagged version of the dependent variable.

items.title: Is there a minimalist but HTMX-aware web server for serving (mostly) static files?
items.body:
I want to make my own website. I was originally using Apache for it because it's one of the most commonly used web servers and I couldn't tell if anything else was better, but after a security scare, I decided to try making my own server, only for a commenter on Super User to slap some sense into me when I tried asking a question about it. After that, I thought that since I had recently discovered the existence of this Stack Exchange site, I would see if it could find something that already exists that does what I want. That includes (in order of most to least important):

  • Must be as secure as possible by default (as opposed to e.g. having to explicitly tell Apache not to just serve random files on the server if given the right request path) or be really easy to secure in this way. (Part of why I wanted to leave Apache was because I couldn't figure out how to make it as secure as I wanted; if I remember correctly, the only helpful-looking resource I could find was so outdated that one part of Apache's own documentation said not to use it, though I was using Debian at the time and I think the resource may have been specific to that.)
  • Must be able to serve static files. The website I want to make will be a combination of a blog and a neal.fun-style collection of small projects. I expect the projects to have their own tech stacks separate from the rest of the site, and the blog will be made entirely out of files that would be static except for the fact that I want to separate out content and metadata that will appear on all pages from content and metadata that's page specific so I don't have to duplicate it. The way I want to do that brings me to...
  • Must be HTMX-aware -- or at least have an extension that makes it so -- without me needing a separate application server behind it. (The design I have in mind for the site means that this HTMX-awareness is the only reason why I might need an application server, and it would be really nice if I didn't need the extra overhead and complexity to do something as simple as working with pieces of webpages.)
  • Must be as simple/minimalist as possible. I imagine that less complexity = less ways to get hacked, so I want it to have as little functionality out of the box as possible other than the features that I need, but I want it to also be extensible so that I can add new features if I later discover that I need them.
  • Must run on Linux, preferably Alpine Linux as I want to use this on the production server (because of, again, minimalism and security). My development environment is Windows so I would like it to run there as well, but if it can't then I am willing to figure out how to set up Docker.
  • Should be free. I have no budget and no good plans to make money from this site other than monetizing some of the projects and using them to subsidize the site. I'm also just cheap lol.
